findings.explanation: The same literal "n1-standard-4" is duplicated in google_notebooks_instance.main.tf:6, google_notebooks_runtime.main.tf:8, and google_workbench_instance.main.tf:8. A caller who needs a larger machine (e.g. for GPU-adjacent memory-heavy notebooks) or a smaller one (cost-sensitive dev environment) cannot right-size any of the three resources without forking the module â€” there is no lever exposed on the module's public interface.
findings.remediation: Add a variable (e.g. machine_type, default "n1-standard-4") and reference var.machine_type in all three resources instead of the literal.
findings.title: machine_type is hardcoded to "n1-standard-4" identically in 3 separate files, with no variable

findings.explanation: name = "legacy-notebook" / "managed-runtime" / "workbench-instance" and account_id = "notebooks-sa" are all literal, unparameterized strings. GCP requires these names to be unique within their scope (project/location), so calling this module a second time in the same project (e.g. a second team, or a dev+staging pair in one project) fails on a name collision. There is no name_prefix or equivalent input to avoid this.
findings.remediation: Add a name_prefix variable (default could reuse one of the current literals for backward compatibility) and interpolate it into every name/account_id in the module. Note: changing an already-deployed name value forces replacement of that resource (name is not updatable in place for these types), so this needs a deliberate decision, not a silent default-on fix, for anyone with an existing deployment.
findings.title: Resource names are hardcoded, so the module cannot be instantiated twice in the same project

findings.explanation: example/examplea's google_kms_crypto_key already uses lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true }, but none of the three compute resources this module creates do. google_notebooks_runtime.main's data_disk also sets auto_delete = true, so an accidental terraform destroy or a forced replacement (e.g. from a future change to an immutable attribute) silently deletes the underlying disk along with any interactive work or local files that were never synced elsewhere.
findings.remediation: Add lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } to all three compute resources, matching the convention already established for the KMS key.
findings.title: No lifecycle.prevent_destroy on any of the three compute resources, unlike the KMS key

findings.explanation: google_notebooks_runtime.main defaults to idle_shutdown = true with a 180-minute timeout even though software_config is never set on it (confirmed against the provider schema) â€” that resource is already safe by default. google_workbench_instance has no equivalent first-class attribute; Workbench's idle-shutdown is configured via instance metadata (the "idle-timeout-seconds" key), which this resource's gce_setup.metadata is never set. An interactive Workbench VM left running overnight or over a weekend accrues compute cost with no automatic stop.
findings.remediation: Set gce_setup.metadata = { "idle-timeout-seconds" = "10800" } (3 hours, adjust to taste) on google_workbench_instance.main.
findings.title: google_workbench_instance has no idle-shutdown configured, unlike google_notebooks_runtime

findings.explanation: disk_size_gb = 100 and disk_type = "PD_STANDARD" are literals with no way for a caller to adjust them â€” either to shrink for a lightweight/cost-sensitive workload or to size up for large datasets, without forking the module.
findings.remediation: Expose data_disk_size_gb (default 100) and data_disk_type (default "PD_STANDARD") variables and reference them.
findings.title: data_disk size and type are hardcoded on the runtime, with no variable

suggested_policies.rationale: google_workbench_instance has no first-class idle-shutdown attribute (unlike google_notebooks_runtime, which defaults to enabled) â€” it's configured via gce_setup.metadata["idle-timeout-seconds"], which is easy to simply never set. Not covered by any existing policy for this resource type (only HLD_GCP_230/CMEK and HLD_GCP_231/public-IP exist).
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_PROPOSED_BP_001
name: Vertex AI Workbench instances should configure idle-timeout metadata
principle: cost
severity: LOW
rationale: |
  Vertex AI Workbench instances have no first-class idle-shutdown attribute.
  Unlike google_notebooks_runtime (which defaults to idle_shutdown = true),
  a Workbench instance left running has no automatic stop unless
  gce_setup.metadata["idle-timeout-seconds"] is explicitly set, so an
  interactive VM left running overnight or over a weekend accrues compute
  cost with nothing to catch it.
remediation: |
  resource "google_workbench_instance" "main" {
    gce_setup {
      metadata = {
        "idle-timeout-seconds" = "10800"
      }
    }
  }
resources:
  google_workbench_instance:
    path: gce_setup.metadata.idle-timeout-seconds
    not_null: true
